title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts enhance colorectal cancer lymphatic metastasis via CLEC11A/LGR5-mediated WNT pathway activation.
authors: Zhang, Chuhan; Pan, Teng; Zhang, Yuyuan; Wu, Yushuai; Zuo, Anning; Liu, Shutong; Ba, Yuhao; Liu, Benyu; Yang, Shuaixi; Chen, Yukang; Xu, Hui; Luo, Peng; Cheng, Quan; Weng, Siyuan; Liu, Long; Zhou, Xing; Ning, Jingyuan; Han, Xinwei; Deng, Jinhai; Liu, Zaoqu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CAFs通过CLEC11A-LGR5激活WNT通路促进结直肠癌淋巴转移，虽用LLM分类器但核心是肿瘤微环境与信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Hypoxia in the tumor microenvironment promotes lymphatic metastasis, yet the role of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in this process remains insufficiently elucidated in colorectal cancer (CRC). In this study, we developed a large language model-based cellular hypoxia-predicting classifier to identify hypoxic CAFs (HCAFs) at single-cell resolution. Our findings revealed that HCAFs enhance CRC lymphatic metastasis by secreting CLEC11A, a protein that binds to the LGR5 receptor on tumor cells, subsequently activating the WNT/beta-catenin signaling pathway. This promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition and lymphangiogenesis, facilitating the spread of tumor cells via the lymphatic system. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the hypoxia-induced transcription factor HIF1A regulates the conversion of normoxic CAFs to HCAFs, driving CLEC11A expression and promoting metastasis. In vivo and vitro experiments confirmed the pro-metastatic role of CLEC11A in CRC, with its inhibition reducing lymphatic metastasis. This effect was markedly reversed by targeting the LGR5 receptor on tumor cells or inhibiting the WNT/beta-catenin pathway, further elucidating the underlying mechanisms of CLEC11A-driven metastasis. These findings underscore the potential of targeting the CLEC11A-LGR5 axis to prevent lymphatic dissemination in CRC. Our study highlights the role of HCAFs in CRC progression and reveals mechanisms of lymphatic metastasis for intervention.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤微环境中的缺氧促进淋巴转移，然而在结直肠癌（CRC）中，癌症相关成纤维细胞（CAFs）在此过程中的作用仍未得到充分阐明。在本研究中，我们开发了一种基于大语言模型的细胞缺氧预测分类器，以单细胞分辨率识别缺氧CAFs（HCAFs）。我们的研究结果显示，HCAFs通过分泌CLEC11A增强CRC的淋巴转移，CLEC11A是一种与肿瘤细胞上LGR5受体结合的蛋白质，随后激活WNT/β-catenin信号通路。这促进了上皮-间质转化和淋巴管生成，从而通过淋巴系统促进肿瘤细胞的扩散。此外，我们证明缺氧诱导的转录因子HIF1A调控常氧CAFs向HCAFs的转化，驱动CLEC11A表达并促进转移。体内和体外实验证实了CLEC11A在CRC中的促转移作用，其抑制可减少淋巴转移。通过靶向肿瘤细胞上的LGR5受体或抑制WNT/β-catenin通路，该效应显著逆转，进一步阐明了CLEC11A驱动转移的潜在机制。这些发现强调了靶向CLEC11A-LGR5轴以预防CRC淋巴扩散的潜力。我们的研究突出了HCAFs在CRC进展中的作用，并揭示了淋巴转移的干预机制。
